forcefields.name: OPLS-UA (2024 parameter file)
references: W. L. Jorgensen et al., J. Phys. Chem. B (2024), doi:10.1021/acs.jpcb.3c06602 (the parameter file)
W. L. Jorgensen, J. D. Madura, C. J. Swenson, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 106, 6638 (1984)
forcefields.source_file: the united-atom types of the 2024 OPLS parameter file (on CAPS's oplsaa2024.json)
forcefields.notes: united atom: hydrogens on carbon fold into their carbons when it is assigned. The table parameterises the united-atom alkanes, alkenes, aromatic CH, alcohols, ethers, sulfur groups, nitriles and chloromethanes. Hydrocarbon terms it never gave (CH-CH2 torsions of branched chains, C=C-C-C and C=C torsions, bends next to an sp2 carbon) come from Jorgensen, Madura & Swenson 1984, Tables I and II ; alcohol and ether terms it never gave (C-C-C-O and secondary or tertiary C-O-H torsions, C-C-O-C torsions, bends at an ether O) from Jorgensen 1986, Tables II and III, and Briggs, Matsui & Jorgensen 1990, Table II and p. 960 (113 bends, 941 torsions in all; bench/ff/open/oplsua2024_supplement.json), the 2024 file's own terms kept. Bends take the papers' fixed angles with the 2024 file's force constants, torsions about C=C the 2024 file's alkene V2 (the papers hold both fixed). O-C-C-O torsions (poly(ethylene oxide), glycols) and O-C-O acetal terms are in none of the papers and are reported as missing, not invented.

typing.evidence: CAPS united-atom rules (bench/ff/make_oplsua2024.py): CH3 typed by the carbons on its neighbour as the 1984 paper defines it; on the polymer library (DP-4 chains) 24 of 114 complete and neutral: every hydrocarbon (polyolefins, polybutadienes, polyisoprenes, polyisobutylene, vinyl cycloalkanes, polynorbornene), poly(vinyl alcohol) and polyoxytetramethylene; poly(ethylene oxide), poly(methylene oxide) and two epoxy resins lack O-C-C-O or acetal terms; 86 left untyped (substituted aromatic C, esters, amides, halogens and other groups without a united-atom type). LAMMPS and GROMACS reproduce CAPS's energies on polypropylene, polybutadiene, cis-polyisoprene, poly(vinyl alcohol) and polyoxytetramethylene oligomers and on the papers' alcohols and diethyl ether.

forcefields.name: Aluminosilicates (Hill & Sauer 1995)
references: J.-R. Hill, J. Sauer, J. Phys. Chem. 99, 9536 (1995)
J.-R. Hill, J. Sauer, J. Phys. Chem. 98, 1238 (1994)
forcefields.source: the paper's Table 8 (cross terms read from the page image); bench/ff/make_hill_sauer1995.py

typing.evidence: the ab initio CFF for silica and zeolite clusters: quartic bonds and angles, torsions, bond-bond, bond-angle, angle-angle and angle-angle-torsion cross terms, the bridging O's out-of-plane term, A_i A_j / r^9 repulsion and bond-increment charges; LAMMPS reproduces CAPS's energies on disilicic acid, a bridging-hydroxyl Si-O(H)-Al cluster, (HO)3Si-O-Al(OH)3 and a cyclotetrasilicic acid

forcefields.name: TraPPE-EH
forcefields.version: the TraPPE database (trappe.oit.umn.edu), explicit-hydrogen family, retrieved October 2026
references: N. Rai, J. I. Siepmann, J. Phys. Chem. B 111, 10790 (2007)
B. L. Eggimann et al., J. Chem. Eng. Data 65, 1330 (2020)
forcefields.source: the TraPPE group's own parameter tables, model by model (trappe.oit.umn.edu), each term with its paper; transcribed by bench/ff/make_trappe_eh.py
forcefields.license: published parameters of the TraPPE papers, cited per term (no file of the site is distributed)

typing.evidence: the 65 TraPPE-EH models (alkanes, amines, amides, nitriles, nitro compounds, aromatics and heteroaromatics), each with its own charges: one CAPS type per symmetry class of a model, typed by a whole-molecule SMARTS (848 / 848 sites as the database types them); every model's bonds, bends and torsions as it lists them (59 / 65 models exact, the rest the database's symmetric-position differences); LAMMPS and GROMACS reproduce CAPS's energies

forcefields.name: All-atom alkanes in silicalite (O'Malley & Catlow 2013)
references: A. J. O'Malley, C. R. A. Catlow, Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys. 15, 19024 (2013)
forcefields.source: the paper's Tables 2 and 3 (read from the page images); bench/ff/make_zeolite_sorbates.py

typing.evidence: alkane C typed by its H count (charges +0.1 per H, each alkane neutral), H, and the formal-charge silica framework (Buckingham Si-O and O-O within 10 A, O-Si-O bends by distance); the paper's torsion (Raj, Sastre & Catlow 1999) not included; LAMMPS reproduces CAPS's energies on alpha-quartz and on alkanes with SiO4, GROMACS on the alkanes

forcefields.name: Methanol in zeolite NaY (Plant, Maurin & Bell 2007)
references: D. F. Plant, G. Maurin, R. G. Bell, J. Phys. Chem. B 111, 2836 (2007)

typing.evidence: Kramer-charge NaY framework with Na (as Ramsahye & Bell), methanol's charges, bonds, bends, torsion and pairs, and its pairs with the framework O and Na; LAMMPS reproduces CAPS's energies on methanol with Na+, AlO4 and SiO4, GROMACS on methanol

forcefields.name: HFA134a (Peguin et al. 2009, FF no. 2)
references: R. P. S. Peguin, G. Kamath, J. J. Potoff, S. R. P. da Rocha, J. Phys. Chem. B 113, 178 (2009)
forcefields.source: the paper's Tables 1 (read from the page image) and 2; bench/ff/make_zeolite_sorbates.py

typing.evidence: CF3CH2F with the paper's FF no. 2 charges and Lennard-Jones terms, OPLS-AA bends and the fitted F-C-C-F and F-C-C-H torsions, no intramolecular pairs; LAMMPS and GROMACS reproduce CAPS's energies

forcefields.name: CHARMM36 CGenFF
references: K. Vanommeslaeghe et al., J. Comput. Chem. 31, 671 (2010)
forcefields.license: no licence stated with the files: built on the user's machine by bench/ff/open/build_charmm.sh, never distributed

typing.evidence: the topology's own residues typed as it types them (bench/ff/validate_rtf_types.py --cap-links): top_all36_cgenff.rtf 9872 / 9872 atoms, 519 / 519 residues (residues with lone pairs left out)

forcefields.notes: Not distributed with CAPS (CHARMM's toppar carries no licence): built on the user's machine by bench/ff/open/build_charmm.sh and loadable by id only where the file is present locally.

forcefields.name: CGenFF 2a5 (J. Comput. Chem. 2010)
references: K. Vanommeslaeghe, E. Hatcher, C. Acharya, S. Kundu, S. Zhong, J. Shim, E. Darian, O. Guvench, P. Lopes, I. Vorobyov, A. D. MacKerell Jr., J. Comput. Chem. 31, 671 (2010), doi:10.1002/jcc.21367
forcefields.source: Supporting Information of the paper, jcc_21367_sm_suppinfo.tgz (doi:10.1002/jcc.21367): par_all36_cgenff.prm and top_all36_cgenff.rtf, CGenFF v. 2a5
forcefields.license: parameter values as published in the Supporting Information of Vanommeslaeghe et al. 2010; CAPS's conversion

typing.evidence: CAPS's CGenFF rules (bench/typing/make_cgenff_rules.py) without the types later releases added, with 2a5's phosphorus and sulfoxide types; the SI's top_all36_cgenff.rtf typed as it types itself for 7471 / 7505 atoms, 371 / 388 residues (bench/ff/validate_rtf_types.py; the other 34 atoms are 2a5 assignments that later releases revised, as CAPS's rules follow, or residues later releases dropped); every residue complete at its integer charge with no missing bonded term, 388 / 388 with the topology's types and 386 / 388 with CAPS's (PRAL and GABD, where CAPS's types differ from 2a5's, each lack one improper, bench/ff/check_rtf_params.py); impropers only where the residues' IMPR records put them (the library's improper_placement, convert_charmm_prm.py --impropers-from-rtf): the 323 they list, 0 missing, 0 extra; LAMMPS and GROMACS reproduce CAPS's energies (Urey-Bradley, 1-4 Lennard-Jones)
